chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Salt Lake City club: Eckstine, Ellington and Henry Armstrong
summary: Horace co-owned the Dixieland club near Salt Lake City, paid stars like Duke Ellington's band (fried chicken, autographs), Billy Eckstine and prizefighter Henry Armstrong to appear, and accompanied Eckstine.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Did you ever have -- do any playing for Billy Eckstine or know him at all?

No, I never did any playing for Billy. Billy happened to have come through Salt Lake City one time when we were fooling around with a night club that business was there, partners with another guy, ownership on a shift deal, and it was a club called Dixieland, out on the highway. And --
Oh, no, this was in the late '30's, I think.
Oh, you were out there then?

Yeah. I'm pretty sure, at that time, because -- wait a minute now. I've got to check back from the time that Fletcher was living because Fletcher was on this, and I think we talked about this earlier when we had jam sessions, we would fly Benny -- Benny Carter out to play

and Henry Armstrong, the prize fighter would come through, and Billy Eckstine would come through, and he did a stint there for us. We'd pay them, and they would make an appearance, and this is the time, I think, that I had Duke Ellington's band come out. They couldn't play, but we had fried chicken out there in the middle of the floor. They signed autographs for the people.
Uh-huh. I know we were talking about that. I can't remember whether we put that on tape or if that was just one of our --

I think we did because we talked about Salt Lake City being a Mormon town, you know, and, boy, they gave us a bad time there because they would block the highway for blocks, especially when we had Duke Ellington there, and Billy Eckstine also. He was a legend. So this is the only time.
Of course, Billy sang there, and I accompanied him. Accompanied him.
